note_sections.t: The patient attends this multidisciplinary consultation to discuss management options following a recent PSA rise to 1.6 ng/mL despite a previously negative biopsy and a PI-RADS 2 magnetic resonance imaging scan.

Recently retired accountant with a complex medical background including long-standing hypertension, atrial fibrillation, moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and documented obesity, currently managed on amlodipine, valsartan, metoprolol, and as-needed salbutamol. He resides with his long-term partner and explicitly declines to nominate a next-of-kin for clinical correspondence. Lower urinary tract symptoms have progressively worsened, yielding an IPSS score of 23/35, which has been partially addressed with tamsulosin. Social history is notable for moderate alcohol consumption averaging 13 units weekly and a consistent routine of light home weight-training twice per week. He prefers morning clinic appointments to accommodate public transport schedules and recently completed a seasonal influenza vaccination alongside a routine chest radiograph at the practice. Incidental findings from his general practice records include a mild, asymptomatic benign liver cyst and a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis managed with oral antihistamines.

Per rectum, the prostate gland feels smooth and symmetrically enlarged without palpable nodules or induration, consistent with a clinical stage of cT1c. General inspection reveals a well-nourished gentleman with stable vital signs, clear lung fields on auscultation despite his known pulmonary history, and no peripheral edema or lymphadenopathy.

next_of_kin: None recorded — patient declines to nominate
